## The Task
Brief: W/task-7-brief.md

## The Findings Under Verification
1. (Important) A user cancel during a tool-call stream must end as `RunError::Cancelled` through `TokioRunner`, and no tool may run. Before round 2, the scratch program /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-helikon/26f7301f-7ced-4a43-84d2-f0ea8bcc0371/scratchpad/cancelrepro printed `RESULT Ok: stop=Completed`. Cause: `controlled` in crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs (biased select, `None => break`) dropped a pending cancel when the inner stream ended first.
2. (Important) The core test comment in crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/tool_calls_not_run.rs falsely claimed the runner maps a stream with no terminal event to Cancelled.

Controller ruling (decided; do not reopen): a text-only stream that ends with no Finish on cancel still gives Ok(Completed) with cut text. That is pre-existing, not caused by this work, and out of scope. Do not count it against finding 1.

## The Fix
Report (fix reports appended at the end): W/task-7-report.md
Fix base: af531df0  Head: 73666f03
Diff file: W/review-af531df0..73666f03.diff

## Verification
- Re-run the scratch program against HEAD in the foreground and report its output (expected `RESULT Err: Cancelled`).
- Check that a run that ended with a real terminal event and was cancelled afterwards still reports success: read `effective_interrupt` / lib.rs ~243-256 and the existing test `prefired_cancel_still_completes_ready_run`; confirm the new `is_cancelled()` check cannot override a terminal event.
- Check a timeout path is not affected (the new code sets Cancelled only when the cancel token fired).
- Check the CHANGELOG bullet is accurate and in plain short sentences.

### Findings
1. ADDRESSED. I re-ran the scratch program (`.../scratchpad/cancelrepro`, `cargo run -q`, foreground) against HEAD 73666f03. Output: `RESULT Err: Cancelled`.
   - The fix is in `controlled`: the `None` arm now sets `RunInterrupt::Cancelled` when `cancel.is_cancelled()`, then breaks.
   - The new test `cancel_during_a_tool_call_stream_is_cancelled` in `run_control.rs` asserts `Err(Cancelled)` and 0 tool calls. I did not run the test suite.
   - Terminal-event override is safe. `effective_interrupt` (core `runner.rs:779`) returns `None` whenever `saw_terminal` is true, and `run` (lib.rs ~243-256) calls it with that flag. A real RunCompleted/RunFailed therefore still wins over the new interrupt value, which is the same path `prefired_cancel_still_completes_ready_run` and `terminal_then_late_cancel_reports_completed` rely on. I read that code and did not run those tests.
   - Timeout is unaffected. The new branch checks only `cancel.is_cancelled()`. The timeout branch is unchanged and sets `TimedOut` in its own select arm.
2. ADDRESSED. The core test comment now reads "The driver ends the stream with no terminal event; the runner then reports the cancel." This matches the behaviour: core produces no terminal, and the runtime-tokio fix produces the Cancelled result.

### CHANGELOG check
The bullet under `[Unreleased] / Fixed` is accurate and uses short, plain sentences. It says a run ends with `RunError::Cancelled` when the agent stream ends after the cancel token fired and no terminal event arrived, and that before this it returned `Ok`.

### New issues in the fix diff
- Critical: none.
- Important: none.
- Minor: the `controlled` doc comment line "A stream that ends after the token fired commits `Cancelled`." does not mention that a terminal event still wins. The inline comment in the code does say so. It is not a defect.

### Out-of-Scope Observations
- The text-only stream that ends on cancel with no Finish still gives `Ok(Completed)` with cut text, per your ruling. The new code does not change that path, because `saw_terminal` handling is the same as before.

### Verdict: All addressed, no new Critical/Important
